lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the completion delivery mechanism (per-component shared completion ring, per-task wait object, or hybrid) and whether io_uring internals are reused or replaced, with wake-up latency measured for each.
rationale: Operation completion is the hinge between kernel scheduling and the runtime and cannot change after SDK code depends on it.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Define the cancellation state machine for in-flight operations that cannot be aborted (DMA already issued, GPU work submitted) and prototype it against a real NVMe read.
rationale: Uniform cancellation is promised, but hardware makes some operations uncancellable and the contract must say what the caller observes.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the deadline and timestamp representation in the ABI (clock domain, resolution, overflow horizon) including how deadlines survive suspend/resume.
rationale: Every operation carries a deadline, so this small decision is stamped into the permanent ABI.

text: Signals are not the primary native notification mechanism; Operation completion and typed channels are.
Define and implement Operation as the fundamental unit of asynchronous outstanding work.
ADR: signals have no native equivalent; specify how termination, cancellation and asynchronous notification are expressed natively.
All native kernel APIs must be asynchronous by default; no native syscall may block the calling execution context as its primary mode.
Do not expose a blocking read()/write() thread-per-call model (block thread, wake thread) as the native I/O interface.
The kernel must expose a submit(operation) primitive that enqueues an Operation for asynchronous execution and returns without waiting for completion.
The kernel must expose a completion delivery mechanism through which finished Operations report results back to the submitting task.

Decide the submission/completion transport for Operations: shared submission and completion rings (io_uring-style), per-Component queues, syscall-per-operation, or a hybrid, and how batching of submissions is expressed.
Decide whether Operations that can complete synchronously (e.g. cached reads) are allowed to complete inline at submit time and how the ABI signals inline completion.
The kernel must support a Read Operation kind against readable objects (File, Channel, MemoryObject-backed sources).
The kernel must support a Write Operation kind against writable objects.
The kernel must support a Receive Operation kind for taking a typed message from a Channel<T>.
The kernel must support a Send Operation kind for placing a typed message on a Channel<T>.
The kernel must support a Connect Operation kind for establishing a connection to a service or NetworkConnection object.
The kernel must support an Accept Operation kind for receiving inbound connections on a listening object.
The kernel must support a Timer Operation kind that completes at or after an absolute or relative deadline.
The kernel must support a Wait Operation kind that completes when a referenced object or set of objects reaches a signalled state.
The kernel must support a DeviceOperation Operation kind for asynchronous requests to Object<Device> instances (including user-space driver backed devices).
The kernel must expose Operation<Result> as a first-class typed object representing one unit of outstanding asynchronous work.
Every Operation must support cancellation by its owner, with a defined result (Cancelled) delivered through the normal completion path.
Every Operation must support completion notification carrying a typed Result or a typed failure.
Every Operation must support a deadline after which it is cancelled or fails with a deadline-exceeded result.
Every Operation must carry a priority that the kernel may use when ordering I/O, IPC, and scheduling work.
Every Operation must have an owner (a Task or TaskGroup) so that ownership can be transferred and cancelled structurally.

Define cancellation semantics for Operations already committed to hardware (in-flight DMA, GPU dispatch, network send): whether cancel waits, fails, or returns best-effort, and how partially completed results are reported.
Prototype deadline enforcement inside the kernel (timer wheel vs hrtimer per Operation) and measure overhead of per-Operation deadlines at high submission rates.
Study io_uring submission/completion rings, linked operations and cancellation for the OPS design.
Asynchronous operation submission and completion via the native ABI (submit, poll/wait, complete).
Principle 5: async is a platform concept; language runtimes bind to kernel Operations rather than reinventing async I/O.
Native Platform layer: Async Operations.
